items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: One who used to give me ideas about different divisions of music was Bush Hall, trumpet player, like I tell you, we played with the Young Tuxedo Band.

ctx.x: That was a Carl Fisher. Carl Fisher. Carl Fisher method, that's right. The old drum method. The old Carl Fisher method. The old stuff stuff One who used to give me ideas about different divisions of music was Bush Hall, trumpet player, like I tell you, we played with the Young Tuxedo Band. And he gave me different pointers about dividing different music. And then I studied my own self, you understand, take the methods and self-practice and just get the ideas, just come to you, listen to other bands play. Then…
When you were young, did you practice very much by yourself on the drums?

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: Lawrence was manager, Bush Hall was leader.

ctx.x: Uh, who did you start playing with? Who, who did you start playing with?

Well we made a band up. A fella by the name of All My Cousins, Bush Hall, trumpet, Paul Ball. He just had got a saxophone. Uh huh. Lawrence Morrell, Aidan Morrell, NFL man they called, uh, we had Raymond Brown first, trombone player. Oh yeah. Myself on the drum. And we named that band. First the name we had called it, called it the Golden Rules, uh, Jazz Band, Golden Rule. Uh huh. Lawrence was manager, Bush Hall was leader. Oh.
That was more of a family band.
